A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICM research and contain the complete main paper and supplementary Sections A–H. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Figure labels missing from v2 text extraction remain visible in rasterized figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-probing, activation-steering and finetuning experiments, including ICM results in Tables 1–5 and additional empirical analyses in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including the quantitative debiasing results and supplementary FLUX, pose-steering and scalability analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and supplementary Sections A–C retain the same activation pooling, external pseudo-labeling, logistic-regression probes, layer selection, normalized steering vectors and selective LoRA finetuning. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain demographic debiasing, implicit-versus-explicit attribute comparisons, USA-presidential identity steering and dog-pose modification. The generated-image scenarios, FairFace attribute evaluation and FFHQ reference data are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Finetuning, Latent Editing, H-Distribution, Latent Direction and DIFFLENS. The corresponding self/cross-attention, general/specific-prompt and selected/random/worst/all-layer comparisons also retain the same participants.

E3.justification: Both specify the same metrics, 500 images per prompt, 2000 generated images for FID and 100 generations for the presidential-steering comparison. Model configurations, preprocessing, training settings and steering start timestep remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same analyses examine attention type, layer selection, general versus specific prompts, steering strength and start timestep. Supplementary analyses of FLUX, pose steering, temporal probe reuse and pooled versus sampled-patch activations are also retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H specifies three images using three different seeds per prompt in both versions. Repeated-run information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged; no uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains ICM steering's gender FD of 0.087 and FID of 122.08, while Table 5 retains Top-20 steering success of 83.0% and CLIP-I of 0.893. Supplementary results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of activations, pseudo-labels and probes, steering equations, diffusion loss and evaluation formulas are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theorems, proofs or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: implicit decisions can be localized through probing, self-attention offers greater attribute separability, and selective intervention improves debiasing while preserving image quality.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretation that self-attention consolidates stochastic cues and that implicit choices differ from explicit conditioning. Discussions of steering-strength artifacts, image-preservation tradeoffs, insufficient target-class samples and pooling-related computational constraints are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code link, probe implementation, Table 6 layer choices and steering strengths, LoRA ranks, optimizer settings, training schedule and prompt templates are identical. Appendix G retains the same runtime, hardware and memory information.

R1.justification: The same 40 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to prompt injection, knowledge localization and existing finetuning or activation-steering approaches does not change.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 29 March 2026 to v2 dated 2 June 2026. Title, authors, prose, terminology, section order and supplementary structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several composite figures, including Figures 1, 5, 7–9 and 11–15, become single raster images in v2, changing rendering sharpness and making their embedded labels non-selectable. Their examples, labels, captions and arrangements are retained; tables and overall page layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific account, empirical evidence and supplementary analyses are unchanged. Figure rasterization substantially reduces file size while slightly softening detail and removing selectable figure labels, but the same evidence remains readable. These production changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall scientific or expository quality.
